# rc.9 release-body pair (sprint-bug-283, KF-064)

The one line of the v2.0.0-rc.9 candidate `release_body` that GitHub stored differently (`candidate-line.txt`, as sent) and the same line as returned by `gh api repos/0xHoneyJar/loa/releases/426462979` (`github-line.txt`). Literal captures from 2026-10-28; never regenerated. `release_body_normalize` must map both to the same string and `release_body_identical` must report `equal` for the pair.

`candidate-line.txt` contains the literal six-character sequences backslash-u-0-0-0-0 and backslash-u-0-0-1-f; `github-line.txt` carries GitHub's stored form, caret `^@` and `^_` after a backslash. Several GitHub surfaces (the pull-request diff view, rendered Markdown) display the candidate file's escapes in caret form too, so the two files can LOOK identical in a browser while `cmp` reports a difference — the fixture test asserts the difference with `cmp` before anything else. Edit these files only with a byte-level tool.

Observed versus assumed mappings: the two observed points are NUL (`\u0000` → `\^@`) and US (`\u001f` → `\^_`), both from this capture. The normaliser extends the rule to the whole C0 range and DEL by the conventional caret notation (`\u0009` → `\^I`, `\u007f` → `\^?`, …); those points are asserted in the caret-table test against the normaliser, not against GitHub. The extension is safe in the accept direction because both sides are normalised: if GitHub leaves one of those escapes alone, the sent and stored bodies still normalise to the same string. If a future refusal names `body (differ …)` on notes that quote such an escape, capture the stored line here as a second observed pair.
